subject.title: Feature Request: Enforce skill execution sandbox when enabled: false

question: Should `skills.entries.<name>.enabled: false` become a hard read/exec denial boundary for skill directories, or should OpenClaw keep it as visibility-only and add a separate strict skill-access policy?
rationale: The code can enforce either shape, but the choice changes security semantics and compatibility for existing trusted setups, so automation should not choose it alone.

options.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard deny
options.body: Disabled skills would be excluded from prompt/status surfaces and blocked centrally from read, write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox materialization paths, with docs and upgrade notes updated accordingly.

options.title: Add a separate strict policy
options.body: Keep current visibility semantics for compatibility while adding an explicit operator-controlled hard-deny policy for untrusted or shared deployments.

options.title: Document current trust model only
options.body: Treat skill folders as trusted code and clarify that disabling a skill only hides it from invocation surfaces, leaving filesystem isolation to sandbox and tool policies.

recommendation.title: Make `enabled:false` a hard deny
recommendation.body: Disabled skills would be excluded from prompt/status surfaces and blocked centrally from read, write/edit/apply_patch, exec, and sandbox materialization paths, with docs and upgrade notes updated accordingly.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a security-boundary and product-semantics call, and Peter Steinberger has adjacent security hardening and project-direction history.
